A material constraint — the staging-area/journal lifecycle for an Evidence-only write set — is stated in a form that is false for two of the sixteen diagnostic ids the same documents place inside its scope. requirements.md:1233-1236 (Security Boundaries) asserts 'A Block whose whole write set is Resolver Evidence never creates that on-disk area at all, because REQ-001 step (m) and REQ-004 fix that one-member write as a direct temp file + fsync + rename, so it is outside this sentence's subject rather than an exception to it', where 'that on-disk area' is the `.resolver-staging/<batch-nonce>/` transaction-journal/pre-image area defined at requirements.md:1206-1208. REQ-004 (requirements.md:594-599) and REQ-001 step (m) (requirements.md:333-336) both place step-(m) Blocks inside the Evidence-only class ('every Block at REQ-001's (0)/(a)/(h)/(i)/(k)/(l)/(m) except (k)'s self-referential case'). But the two step-(m) Blocks are `artifact-publication-failed`, whose own REQ-002 row (requirements.md:385) defines it as a failure caught 'during this invocation's own publication transaction's Prepare/Journal/Commit phases' with journal-based rollback, and `post-publication-generation-mismatch` (requirements.md:386), which fires only after every rename succeeded and rolls back via 'the transaction's own journal'. Both therefore necessarily created the on-disk area; AC-039 and AC-049 require fixtures that depend on it existing. DOWNSTREAM FAILURE MODE: a task author or verifier deriving a staging-lifecycle invariant from the Security Boundaries sentence ('assert `.resolver-staging/` was never created on an Evidence-only Block') writes a fixture that AC-039/AC-049's journal-rollback fixtures contradict; the stated justification for why the direct write is 'outside this sentence's subject' does not hold for those two ids, even though the conclusion is separately supportable (the Block-record Evidence is never placed in the on-disk area). CORROBORATING SECOND INSTANCE, same constraint: the step enumeration '(0)/(a)/(h)/(i)/(k)/(l)/(m)' is offered at requirements.md:333-336 and 594-599 as coextensive with 'when Evidence is the only thing this invocation writes', but omits every Evidence-only Block raised at steps (b), (d), (e), between (e) and (f), and within the (f)-(g) sweep — at minimum `project-context-validation-failed`, `canonicalizer-invocation-failed`, `affected-component-resolution-failed`, `registry-validation-failed`, `contract-discovery-failed`, the ruling-C(1) `snapshot-generation-mismatch` step-(e) site (requirements.md:384; AC-057 requires Evidence written there), and the ruling-C(2) `dependency-output-malformed` absent-component sub-trigger (requirements.md:380; AC-058 requires Evidence written there). REQ-004's two-armed dichotomy ('alongside the rest of a track's output set' vs the enumerated list) leaves those seven ids' write mechanism unstated, even though AC-012 requires Evidence for each. WHY SPEC REVIEW: both instances are misstatements inside the Phase-1 frozen constraint text produced by the D(2) narrowing, not design choices. WHY MAJOR NOT CRITICAL: the operative rule is independently recoverable step-agnostically from requirements.md:979-986 (Roles and Permissions, 'whenever Resolver Evidence is the invocation's whole write set') and from the stated rationale ('a one-member write set has no sibling to be inconsistent with'), so an implementer can still decide; the harm is downstream mismatch in derived invariants and fixtures, not unreviewability.
